arxiv-1904-11266.title: Discrete Optimal Graph Clustering
arxiv-1904-11266.creator: Yudong Han, Lei Zhu, Zhiyong Cheng, Jingjing Li, Xiaobai Liu
arxiv-1904-11266.description: Abstract Graph based clustering is one of the major clustering methods. Most of it work in three separate steps: similarity graph construction, clustering label relaxing and label discretization with k-means. Such common practice has three disadvantages: 1) the predefined similarity graph is often fixed and may not be optimal for the subsequent clustering.

arxiv-2011-05067.title: TRACKING CHANGE-POINTS IN MULTIVARIATE EXTREMES Corresponding Author. Postal address: School of Human Sciences and Technology, IE University, Calle Maria de Molina 6, 28006 Madrid, Spain. Email: manuele.leonelli@ie.edu
arxiv-2011-05067.creator: Miguel de Carvalho
arxiv-2011-05067.description: Abstract In this paper we devise a statistical method for tracking and modeling change-points on the dependence structure of multivariate extremes. The methods are motivated by and illustrated on a case study on crypto-assets. keywords : Change-point; Crypto-assets; Fat tail; Multivariate extreme values; Time-varying extreme-value copula. jel classification : C46, F38, G01. 1.

arxiv-2207-09345.title: Local to global principles for homomorphisms of abelian schemes
arxiv-2207-09345.creator: by Wojciech Gajda, Sebastian Petersen
arxiv-2207-09345.description: Abstract Let A and B be abelian varieties defined over the function field k(S) of a smooth algebraic variety S/k. We establish criteria, in terms of restriction maps to subvarieties of S, for existence of various important classes of k(S) -homomorphisms from A to B, e.g., for existence of k(S) -isogenies.

arxiv-2211-11598.title: Hilbert Series and Operator Counting on the Higgs Effective Field Theory
arxiv-2211-11598.creator: Hao Sun, Yi-Ning Wang, Jiang-Hao Yu
arxiv-2211-11598.description: Abstract We present a systematic procedure for determining the Hilbert series that counts the number of independent operators in the Higgs effective field theory. After removing the redundancies from equation-of-motion and integration-by-part, we provide an algorithm of treating the redundancy from the operators involving in spurion fields parametrizing the custodial symmetry breaking.

arxiv-2307-13286.title: Public and private beliefs under disinformation in social networks
arxiv-2307-13286.creator: Diana Riazi, Giacomo Livan
arxiv-2307-13286.description: Abstract We develop a model of opinion dynamics where agents in a social network seek to learn a ground truth among a set of competing hypotheses. Agents in the network form private beliefs about such hypotheses by aggregating their neighbors’ publicly stated beliefs, in an iterative fashion.

arxiv-2307-14632.title: Metric-Based In-context Learning: A Case Study in Text Simplification
arxiv-2307-14632.creator: Subha Vadlamannati, Gözde Gül Şahin
arxiv-2307-14632.description: Abstract In-context learning (ICL) for large language models has proven to be a powerful approach for many natural language processing tasks. However, determining the best method to select examples for ICL is nontrivial as the results can vary greatly depending on the quality, quantity, and order of examples used.

arxiv-2312-07274.title: Factorisation Quantum Groups
arxiv-2312-07274.creator: Alexei Latyntsev
arxiv-2312-07274.description: Abstract A BSTRACT : We develop vertex and factorisation algebra analogues of the theory of quasitriangular bialgebras. Analogously to the classical theory, we prove their categories of representations are controlled by spectral R -matrices. In the vertex algebra case this generalises previous notions due to Etingof-Kazhdan and Frenkel-Reshetikhin. Finally we give examples, including Borcherds twists and homology vertex algebras. 0.

arxiv-2406-03487.title: Analyzing LLM Behavior in Dialogue Summarization: Unveiling Circumstantial Hallucination Trends
arxiv-2406-03487.creator: Sanjana Ramprasad, Elisa Ferracane, Zachary C. Lipton
arxiv-2406-03487.description: Abstract Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have considerably advanced the capabilities of summarization systems. However, they continue to face concerns about hallucination . While prior work has evaluated LLMs extensively in news domains, most evaluation of dialogue summarization has focused on BART-based models, leaving a gap in our understanding of their faithfulness.

arxiv-2411-07472.title: Semi-Truths: A Large-Scale Dataset of AI-Augmented Images for Evaluating Robustness of AI-Generated Image detectors
arxiv-2411-07472.creator: Anisha Pal, Julia Kruk, Mansi Phute, Manognya Bhattaram, Diyi Yang, Duen Horng Chau, Judy Hoffman
arxiv-2411-07472.description: Abstract Text-to-image diffusion models have impactful applications in art, design, and entertainment, yet these technologies also pose significant risks by enabling the creation and dissemination of misinformation. Although recent advancements have produced AI-generated image detectors that claim robustness against various augmentations, their true effectiveness remains uncertain. Do these detectors reliably identify images with different levels of augmentation?

arxiv-2502-06210.title: Achieving Deep Continual Learning via Evolution
arxiv-2502-06210.creator: Aojun Lu, Junchao Ke, Chunhui Ding, Jiahao Fan, Jiancheng Lv, Yanan Sun
arxiv-2502-06210.description: Abstract Deep neural networks, despite their remarkable success, remain fundamentally limited in their ability to perform Continual Learning (CL). While most current methods aim to enhance the capabilities of a single model, Inspired by the collective learning mechanisms of human populations, we introduce Evolving Continual Learning (ECL), a framework that maintains and evolves a diverse population of neural network models.

arxiv-2601-20148.title: LogSieve: Task-Aware CI Log Reduction for Sustainable LLM-Based Analysis CCS: Software and its engineering Software testing and debugging CCS: Software and its engineering Software maintenance tools CCS: Computing methodologies Information extraction
arxiv-2601-20148.creator: Marcus Emmanuel Barnes, Taher A. Ghaleb, Safwat Hassan
arxiv-2601-20148.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Marcus Emmanuel Barnes, Taher A. Ghaleb, Safwat Hassan. Logs are essential for understanding Continuous Integration (CI) behavior, particularly for diagnosing build failures and performance regressions. Yet their growing volume and verbosity make both manual inspection and automated analysis increasingly costly, time-consuming, and environmentally costly. While prior work has explored log compression, anomaly detection, and LLM-based log analysis, most efforts target structured system logs rather than the unstructured, noisy, and verbose logs typical of CI workflows.

While there is an increasing body of evidence demonstrating beneficial effects of IF on blood lipids and other health outcomes in the overweight and obese, l

pmc-10558543.title: Morphogenetic metasurfaces: unlocking the potential of Turing patterns
pmc-10558543.creator: Thomas Fromenteze, Okan Yurduseven, Chidinma Uche, Eric Arnaud, David R. Smith, Cyril Decroze
pmc-10558543.description: The reaction-diffusion principle imagined by Alan Turing in an attempt to explain the structuring of living organisms is leveraged in this work for the procedural synthesis of radiating metasurfaces. The adaptation of this morphogenesis technique ensures the growth of anisotropic cellular patterns automatically arranged to satisfy local electromagnetic constraints, facilitating the radiation of waves controlled in frequency, space, and polarization.

pmc-11401244.title: Menopausal symptoms and utilization of menopausal hormone therapy among women aged 40–60 years in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia: a cross-sectional study
pmc-11401244.creator: Tewodros Getahun Asfaw, Rahel Demissew Gebreyohannes, Milcah Temesgen Tesfaye
pmc-11401244.description: BackgroundThe onset of menopause leads to diminished estrogen exposure, resulting in a high morbidity burden related to menopausal symptoms. Menopausal hormonal therapy is an effective therapy that offers more advantages than disadvantages for women aged less than 60 years or who have had menopause for less than 10 years.

pmc-11440184.title: Effects of reducing sedentary behaviour on back pain, paraspinal muscle insulin sensitivity and muscle fat fraction and their associations: a secondary analysis of a 6-month randomised controlled trial
pmc-11440184.creator: Jooa Norha, Tanja Sjöros, Taru Garthwaite, Saara Laine, Tiina Verho, Virva Saunavaara, Kirsi Laitinen, Noora Houttu, Jussi Hirvonen, Henri Vähä-Ypyä, Harri Sievänen, Eliisa Löyttyniemi, Tommi Vasankari, Kari Kalliokoski, Ilkka Heinonen
pmc-11440184.description: ObjectivesSedentary behaviour (SB) is a plausible intervention target for back pain mitigation. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the effects of a 6-month SB reduction intervention on back pain and related disability outcomes, and paraspinal muscle (ie, erector spinae and transversospinales separately) insulin sensitivity (glucose uptake, GU) and muscle fat fraction (FF).

pmc-11678435.title: Construction and Experimental Validation of Embedded Potential Functions for Ta-Re Alloys
pmc-11678435.creator: Haohao Miao, Xuehuan Xia, Yonghao Fu, Jing Yan, Lu Li, Hongzhong Cai, Xiao Wang, Chengling Wu, Zhaolin Zhan, Xian Wang, Zhentao Yuan
pmc-11678435.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Ta/Re layered composite material is a high-temperature material composed of the refractory metal tantalum (Ta) as the matrix and high-melting-point, high-strength rhenium (Re) as the reinforcement layer. It holds significant potential for application in aerospace engine nozzles. Developing the Ta/Re potential function is crucial for understanding the diffusion behavior at the Ta/Re interface and elucidating the high-temperature strengthening and toughening mechanism of Ta/Re layered composites.

pmc-12432098.title: The Fifth Vital Sign in the First 1000 Days: Early Relational Health
pmc-12432098.creator: İclal Ayrancı Sucaklı, Sıddika Songül Yalçın
pmc-12432098.description: Early childhood development forms the cornerstone for a healthy, fulfilling, and productive life. Research in health psychology and longevity highlights that social relationships are the most significant determinant of lifelong health and development. Among these, early attachment between children and caregivers, bolstered by positive experiences and nurturing environments, is pivotal for optimal growth, development, and well-being.

pmc-12516617.title: Population health impacts from the taxation of salt and sugar in the United Kingdom
pmc-12516617.creator: Patricia Eustachio Colombo, James Milner, Silvia Pastorino, Rosemary Green
pmc-12516617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Objective:To estimate the potential health benefits from the reduction in consumption of salt and sugar following the introduction of a proposed tax on salt and sugar in the United Kingdom (UK).Design:Epidemiological modelling study. Life table modelling was used to estimate the expected population health benefits from the reduction in consumption of salt and sugar for four scenarios, each reflecting different manufacturer and consumer responses the proposed tax.

pmc-12555335.title: Effectiveness of Simulation-Based CPR Training Among Medical Students: A Pilot study
pmc-12555335.creator: R Sánchez Bermúdez, J E Villegas Domiínguez, N A Hernández Fernández, K Azuara Díaz, F Ruiz Garcia, Y R Sosa Gonzalez
pmc-12555335.description: IntroductionImproving CPR training among medical students is a key public health strategy to reduce preventable deaths from cardiac arrest, especially in those about to begin their internship year in hospital settings. Identifying the most effective training approach is essential, taking advantage of the technological resources available in universities.

pmc-12595119.title: MoringaLeafNet: A multi-class leaf disease dataset for precision agriculture and deep learning research
pmc-12595119.creator: Sabit Ahamed Preanto, Tapon Paul, Abid Khan, Md Hasan Imam Bijoy
pmc-12595119.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Moringa Oleifera, which has outstanding nutritional and health benefits, is prized around the world because its leaves are rich in essential vitamins, antioxidants, and minerals that support digestion, help the immune system, and fight inflammation. Still, growing Moringa can be difficult because diseases such as Yellow Leaf, Bacterial Leaf Spot, and Cercospora Leaf Spot are hard to detect early and spread fast, leading to a lot of damage.

pmc-12752596.title: High‐Temperature Single‐Photon Emission From Covalently Functionalized van der Waals Heterostructures
pmc-12752596.creator: S. Carin Gavin, Hsun‐Jen Chuang, Anushka Dasgupta, Moumita Kar, Kathleen M. McCreary, Sung‐Joon Lee, M. Iqbal Bakti Utama, Chunxi Zhou, Xiangzhi Li, George C. Schatz, Tobin J. Marks, Mark C. Hersam, Berend T. Jonker, Nathaniel P. Stern
pmc-12752596.description: Two‐dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) such as tungsten diselenide (WSe2) are attractive nanomaterials for quantum information applications due to single‐photon emission (SPE) from intrinsic atomic defects. Defect and strain engineering techniques have been developed to produce high purity, deterministically placed SPE in WSe2.

pmc-13052088.title: Aortic Valve Perforation in Pediatric Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis: A Case Report
pmc-13052088.creator: Libor Svoboda, Martin Scholten, Corinna Jugel, Johanna Buschner, Christian Schürer, Alexandra Kiess
pmc-13052088.description: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis, formerly Wegener's granulomatosis, is a rare antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)–associated vasculitis primarily affecting the respiratory tract and kidneys. Cardiovascular involvement, particularly valvular disease, is rare, especially in pediatric patients. We report a case of a 12‐year‐old boy newly diagnosed with granulomatosis with polyangiitis, who developed an aortic valve perforation.

pmc-13251003.title: Network analysis of school connectedness and psychological crisis among university students
pmc-13251003.creator: Ding Zhang, Nan Gao, Yao Wang, Xiaoqian Liu, Haoran Peng, Shihan Hu, Xuelan Liu
pmc-13251003.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveWith the rising incidence of psychological crisis among university students, the research focus has gradually shifted from a symptom-based to a protective-factor perspective, in which school connectedness is considered a potential protective factor.

pmc-13284702.title: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate post hospital discharge to prevent hyperkalaemia: phase 4, randomized CONTINUITY trial
pmc-13284702.creator: James O Burton, María J Izquierdo, Cecilia Linde, Nicolás R Robles, Manish M Sood, Alaster M Allum, James M Eudicone, Magnus Dahl, Alpesh N Amin
pmc-13284702.description: Background and hypothesisHyperkalaemia is common and potentially life-threatening in individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD). While sodium zirconium cyclosilicate (SZC) is used in the hospital setting for hyperkalaemia management, few patients are discharged with a continuing prescription, leaving them at risk of recurrent hyperkalaemia and rehospitalization.

pmc-13315668.creator: Emre Demirel, Ozan Çolak, Mustafa Aktaş, Muhammet Buğra Öcal, Özgür Çıtlak, Emel Tahir, Özgür Kemal, Senem Çengel Kurnaz

pmc-13408490.title: Prevalence and its associated factors of cancer-related fatigue among liver cancer patients: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13408490.creator: Xuejiao Xiong, Qian Wang, Li Wang, Biying Fu, Min Tu
pmc-13408490.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study aimed to identify the prevalence of CRF and its associated factors in liver cancer patients. A cross-sectional study was conducted at a major teaching hospital in Sichuan Province, China, between October and December 2025. A total of 315 liver cancer patients were recruited to complete a survey comprising the demographic and clinical information form, the Cancer Fatigue Scale (CFS), the FRAIL Scale, the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS), and the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI).

pmc-13593949.title: Agreement of Over-the-Counter Continuous Glucose Monitors With Capillary-Meter Glucose in Young Adults Without Diabetes
pmc-13593949.creator: Navneet Prakash, Andrea H Barrows, Matthew Stults-Kolehmainen, Andrew J Loza, Marcus W Kilpatrick, Garrett I Ash
pmc-13593949.description: Background:Over-the-counter continuous glucose monitors (OTC CGMs) are increasingly used by individuals without diabetes for lifestyle modification, weight management, athletics, and metabolic screening, and have potential as an affordable tool for glucose data collection in research. However, accuracy and agreement data in their intended populations are limited. No independent study has yet evaluated OTC CGM accuracy or agreement.

pmc-13677685.title: Efficient conversion of syngas into sustainable aviation fuel
pmc-13677685.creator: Jian Han, Shenggang Li, Guofei Shen, Wei Liu, Jian Zhang, Dong Fang, Bohui Ye, Yifan Sun, Haofan Wang, Xianni Bu, Chengguang Yang, Hao Wang, Haiyan Yang, Jiong Li, Yuhan Sun, Peng Gao
pmc-13677685.description: Fischer−Tropsch synthesis to paraffinic kerosene is a crucial pathway to obtain sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), but a more efficient catalyst is needed for practical applications. Here, we report a cobalt-manganese catalyst supported on tetrapropylammonium hydroxide-etched Beta zeolites that breaks the long-standing activity-selectivity trade-off. The obtained catalyst achieves 82.8% CO conversion and 67.5% C8−16 selectivity, yielding a high productivity.
